## Triage outcome — task 10256 (2026-11-05, lane code-p)

**Verdict: CONFIRMED as a valid standalone design ticket — routed with its tier-2 dependency recorded. It should not be designed before the vocabulary tickets settle.**

**Fresh verification (2026-11-05):** issue #5853 OPEN, labels task/triage + queue/queued + app/id — no hard-stop labels, no prior comments beyond the tracking link. Parent #5679 (Markup & styling model for programs-as-websites) is OPEN and was triaged today (task 10112, lane code-h): grandparent #2146 is CLOSED, the gap pass filed all seven children #5849–#5855, all OPEN. No `doc/` record covers custom GUI rendering overrides (doc/ hits are a screen-render alignment feature note and a remote-GUI runbook — neither is this design), and no other issue covers it.

**Ordering (from the parent triage, task 10112 — dependencies, not a schedule):**
1. **#5849 (semantic markup vocabulary v1) + #5850 (style assertion vocabulary) first** — every rendering ticket maps from the settled vocabularies.
2. **#5851 / #5852 / #5853 next, in parallel** — each maps the vocabularies to one target class; this ticket is the custom-target one.
3. #5854 (per-target customisation) after the rendering tickets; #5855 (pipeline & conformance) last.

So #5853's design start is gated on the #5849/#5850 decision records existing — not on Drew, and not on its tier-2 siblings #5851/#5852.

**Boundary discipline for the design:**
- Settle only: wholly custom presentations (image buttons, drawn controls) as FIRST-CLASS overrides of the standard renderings — the override mechanism, what a custom presentation declares, and how it composes with the parent's semantic markup + style-assertion model.
- Do NOT re-decide the parent model; conflicts get recorded on #5679, not forked.
- Do NOT swallow #5854: override maps and asset substitution as a per-target customisation system are #5854's scope, defined against the rendering tickets afterwards. This ticket settles the custom-presentation mechanism #5854 will reference.
- Deliverable is the ticket's own decision record (chosen shape, alternatives rejected and why, implementation invariants), on the issue or in a `doc/` record linked from it. Implementation timing is a separate later decision.

**Routing:** follow-up design task enqueued with the tier-2 dependency stated in its packet (a worker claiming it early must check #5849/#5850 state first and park with that reason if the records do not yet exist).
